MINUTES
  PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MEETING
  JOINT MEETING WITH THE EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE
  AUGUST 20, 2019

  A special joint meeting of the Park and Activities Commission and the Equestrian Committee of
  the City of Rolling Hills Estates was called to order at 7:08 p.m. at Ernie Howlett Park, 25851
  Hawthorne Blvd., Rolling Hills Estates, California by CHAIR RETZ. CHAIR RETZ deferred to
  COUNCILMEMBER and EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE CHAIR HUFF to Chair the meeting.

  2.  ROLL CALL

  COMMISSIONERS PRESENT:  Bain, Ciarolla, McCormick, Retz, Romanelli

  COMMISSIONERS ABSENT:  Persichina, Pope

  COMMITTEE MEMBERS PRESENT:  Huff, Ciarolla, Martin, Shinn, Silvano

  COMMITTEE MEMBERS ABSENT:  Brtis, Dean-Porter, Zigrang

  STAFF PRESENT:  Alexa Davis, Assistant City Manager
  Michael Goldsmith, Maintenance Superintendent
  Cynthia Morquecho, Comm. Services Supervisor

  3.  BUSINESS ITEMS

  A.  COWBOY MOUNTED SHOOTING DEMONSTRATION

  B.  CONSIDERATION OF CALIFORNIA DESPERADOS AND COWBOY MOUNTED
  SHOOTING ASSOCIATION - MOUNTED SHOOTING COMPETITION EVENT AT
  ERNIE HOWLETT PARK

  COMMUNITY SERVICES SUPERVISOR MORQUECHO provided a brief overview per
  the agenda material. Event organizers, Brenda Caropino and Mark Caropino, provided
  an expanded overview of her personal involvement in the community and further explained
  the proposed event. Mr. Caropino detailed the way shots are done with gun powder which
  breaks balloon through its heat not projectiles. Ms. Caropino explained that they anticipate
  25 participants at this proposed event.

  EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE (EC) MEMBER SILVANO asked how many rounds and
  during what timeframe would shots be fired. MS. CAROPINO responded that there are a
  series of four to five rounds with 10 balloons each from 10 am to 2:30 or 3 pm.

  EC MEMBER SILVANO stated that is over 1,000 balloons and shots.

  MS. CAROPINO further detailed that there is discussion and set-up between rounds and
  riders appear every two minutes.

  EC CHAIR HUFF asked if there are local participants.

JOINT PARK AND ACTIVITIES /EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MEETING MINUTES  1
AUGUST 20, 2019
   MS. CAROPINO confirmed there are four to five local participants and she is hoping this
  event will garner interest. She expressed the hope of holding a clinic at the park in the
  future. She further explained that a similar activity has been done with local Sheriff’s
  Posse horses without issue.

  She proceeded to pass around an unloaded gun to Commission and Committee members
  for view.

  EC MEMBER asked if anyone could have snuck live ammunition in the guns.

  MS. CAROPINO responded no.

  PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSIONER (PAC) ROMANELLI asked who regulates the
  ammunition.

  MR. CAROPINO explained that only three to four companies make that type of
  ammunition and that loading and unloading is done at a staging area where organizers
  provide the ammunition directly to participants.

  EC MEMBER SILVANO asked for confirmation that the City Attorney has reviewed the
  event to allow these type of firearms.

  ASSISTANT CITY MANAGER responded that the City Attorney believes that this event is
  similar to a film shoot where guns with live ammunition are not used and therefore is
  permitted at Public Parks through City approval.

  EC MEMBER SILVANO stated that due to the environment of the world, she is concerned
  about inviting a gun event into the City.

  PAC CHAIR RETZ asked if there can be a procedure in place to ensure non-competition
  horse owners be made aware. ASSISTANT CITY MANAGER affirmed.

  MR. CARAPINO proceeded to the arena for a demonstration. For the first round,
  Commission and Committee members stayed adjacent to the tennis office to hear the
  demonstration. For the second round, Commission and Committee members proceeded
  to the arena to observe the demonstration closer.

  MEMBER OF THE PUBLIC PAM SCHACHTER noted that after the first shot was fired,
  several birds in and around the park flew away.

  EC MEMBER SHINN stated the noise was too loud and believes it will travel. She further
  stated she is not comfortable with guns coming into the City.

  EC MEMBER SILVANO stated that she was not a fan of bringing guns into the City with
  the climate of our world currently. She said she is not as concerned with the noise.

  MS. CAROPINO explained that the audience is normally people who are familiar with the
  event.

JOINT PARK AND ACTIVITIES /EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MEETING MINUTES  2
AUGUST 20, 2019
   EC MEMBER MARTIN stated that he supports the greater horse community and this event
  does that and he is willing to give it a try.

  EC/PAC MEMBER CIAROLLA stated that she is willing to give this event a try. She
  explained that the sound is no louder than fireworks which some horses will react to and
  some will not.

  PAC CHAIR RETZ stated that he is torn. He explained that he loves the horse community
  and encourages horse events but is concerned about guns, even with blanks fired. He
  further explained that even when notifications exist, some are still unaware of an event
  happening.

  PAC MEMBER MCCORMICK stated he was uncomfortable with 25-30 participants all
  carrying guns.

  PAC MEMBER BAIN stated she was not comfortable with so many guns at a public park
  with children present.

  PAC MEMBER ROMANELLI stated that he would be willing to approve the event with
  specific checks and balances and it was unfortunate that a few bad actors have changed
  the perception on responsible gun use.

  EC CHAIR HUFF stated that she appreciated the event organizers time in demonstrating
  the event but agreed that given the environment in our country currently, many people are
  skittish about guns. She further explained that looking at a wider city benefit and the people
  of the greater community she cannot support this event.

  MEMBER OF THE PUBLIC BOB KRUEGER stated that he works at the Ernie Howlett
  Park Tennis Courts and explained loud noises, such as what is being proposed for this
  event, are very distracting to tennis players. For example, the drums used at the finish line
  at a recent race event.

  EC CHAIR HUFF CALLED FOR A VOTE TO APPROVE THE CALIFORNIA
  DESPERADOS COWBOY MOUNTED SHOOTING EVENT REQUEST FOR ERNIE
  HOWLETT PARK.

  THE VOTE OF THE EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE WAS AS FOLLOWS:
  Ayes: Martin, Ciarolla
  Noes: Huff, Shinn, Silvano
  Absent: Brtis, Dean-Porter, Zigrang

  THE VOTE OF THE PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION WAS AS FOLLOWS:
  Ayes: Ciarolla, Romanelli
  Noes: Bain, McCormick, Retz
  Absent: Persichina, Pope

JOINT PARK AND ACTIVITIES /EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MEETING MINUTES  3
AUGUST 20, 2019
   Based upon the vote outcome, EC CHAIR HUFF requested that staff proceed to the City
  Council with a recommendation denying the California Desperados Cowboy Mounted
  Shooting event request for Ernie Howlett Park.

  15.  ADJOURNMENT

  EC CHAIR HUFF adjourned the meeting at 7:53 pm.

  Respectfully submitted,

  __________________________
  Alexa Davis
  Assistant City Manager

JOINT PARK AND ACTIVITIES /EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MEETING MINUTES  4
AUGUST 20, 2019
